Definition: from G575 and the middle voice of G5412; to unload:--unlade.
BiblicalUsage: Once, on Paul's last voyage to Jerusalem. The ship sailed into Syria and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unlade her burden — the word is the unloading of cargo at the end of a leg of the journey.
TheologicalSignificance: A sailor's word, and nothing more: the cargo comes off at Tyre so the ship can go on.
